text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000197's 99215 share far exceeds what patient complexity predicts, including in low-complexity strata, but documentation is too thin to confirm or refute support for the billed level.","leaning":"pattern_consistent_with_upcoding","interpretation":"The elevated 99215 rate runs above the all-provider share in every complexity stratum, not just among sicker patients. A large portion of the 99215s fall on patients with zero or one chronic condition, often with routine diagnoses such as hyperlipidemia, hypertension or abdominal pain (e.g., C0098741, C0098757, C0098853, C0098872). That pattern is consistent with upcoding rather than a high-acuity panel. Some of the sampled high-complexity 99215s (e.g., C0098702, C0098728) look clinically plausible. The two documented 99215s, C0098702 and C0098858, were supported at high MDM, but two charts are far too few to judge. C0098858 is a single-condition depression visit, so its high-MDM note deserves a closer look for cloned or templated content. That concern is reinforced, weakly, by the 5 moderate-plus data-reviewed notes with no lab or test line on the claim. A reviewer should first request records for the low-complexity 99215 claims listed in the packet. They should then compare those notes against the documented MDM and time elements, and check for templated language across patients."}
